A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sitaxentan, a potent inhibitor of BSEP, causes liver injury through a complex mechanism involving mitochondrial dysfunction, cell toxicity, and CVB.
multiple compound-related adverse properties contribute to liver injury caused by endothelin receptor antagonism.
sitaxentan is a high-risk, low-impact drug, bosentan is a moderate-risk, moderate-impact drug, and ambrisentan is a low-risk, low-impacts drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single assay is not sufficient to identify the mechanism(s) of drug-induced liver injury.

multiple mechanisms of toxicity may contribute to liver injury caused by endothelin receptor antagonism, but that the risk for liver toxicity is markedly lower for ambrisentan than for sitaxentan or bosentan.
